briefFidelity: The brief asks for a colony of cells, biological rather than geometric, rounded forms, in verdigris and bone over deep ink, with growth and retreat as the whole market story. Two of those four clauses land and two do not, and the two that fail are the ones the brief leans on hardest. The palette is a clean hit: writing blind I called it desaturated sea-green, bone-white and near-black and reached for the word mineral unprompted, which is the briefs own word. The failure is form. The green ellipse mass is two or three lobes, not a colony, and nothing in it buds generationally - there is no chain of smaller members accreting outward in any of the twelve, only a peanut in 9011, 9369, 10801, 10264 and a slightly rounder peanut in 9548. Worse, every piece of actual incident is rectilinear: the bone layer is rotated rectangles and long thin slabs, and the scatter is squares and diamonds. Blind, before I had read a word of the brief, I described 9190, 10443 and 10980 as pick-up-sticks and asterisks, 10622 as opaque rectangles in near-horizontal courses, and 9727 as a column of squares and a file of diamonds. That is the exact word the brief forbids - geometric - applied by an unprompted reader to the layer carrying all the drawing. Rounded forms clustered and overlapping is delivered only by the background mass, and in 9906, 10085 and 10622 even that is gone, leaving a frame of grey and cream rectangles with no colony in it at all. This is the briefs own failure example inverted: commissioned biological, reads constructed.
composition: There is a real focal hierarchy and it is deliberate: a bright bone knot sitting on a darker green body, brightest where the translucent slabs overprint, so the eye goes to the centre first in 9011, 9369, 9548, 10264 and 10801 without ambiguity. That is the strongest thing on the sheet after the palette. The frame, though, is barely used. Eleven of twelve tokens float a centred mass in a dark surround with even margins on all four sides, and the composition would be unchanged if the canvas were 10 percent larger. 9727 is the one token that engages its edges deliberately, with a hard column of squares down the left and a file of diamonds down the right, and it is the most composed frame here. 10622 also reaches the edges but by running slabs off all four of them, which reads as a crop of a larger picture rather than a decision. Within the centred ones the pale rectangles parked half on and half off the green body at left and right in 9011 and 9369 are the weakest passages - they neither anchor the frame nor belong to the knot.
collectionCoherence: Nine of the twelve are unmistakably one project: identical three-colour palette, identical construction grammar of soft translucent ellipse mass plus hard bone slabs plus scatter squares, identical centre of gravity. 9011, 9369, 9548, 9190, 9727, 10264, 10443, 10801 and 10980 would sit together on a wall without argument. The other three break it. 9906 has only a smear of green behind its bars, 10085 has no green mass visible at all, and 10622 is a different work altogether - large opaque grey and cream rectangles stacked in horizontal courses across the whole frame with one green fragment surviving at the lower left. Reading blind I flagged 9906 and 10085 as looking like a render that failed to draw its background layer, which is the shape of the problem: the element that carries the collections identity is the green colony, and three tokens in twelve, a quarter of the sheet, have effectively lost it.
palette: The best axis. Verdigris green, bone cream and a deep blue-black ink, and it does feel damp and mineral rather than bright - I described the green mass as stone and the bone cluster as a mineral inclusion before I knew those were the briefs own terms. The ground genuinely supports rather than competes: the near-black is a hair off neutral toward blue, which keeps the green from going acid and lets the cream read as the only true light in the frame. The contrast range is doing real work rather than making noise, because the alpha overprinting earns its mid-tones - the double-exposed darker green ghost behind the mass in 9011, 9369 and 10801, and the brightening where four or five bone slabs stack in 9548 and 10264, are both produced by the layering rather than added as extra colours. The one impurity is the grey of the scatter squares in 9727, 10085 and 10622: it is a fourth family, neither verdigris nor bone, and in 10622 where it dominates the frame it reads as unfinished rather than chosen.
seedVariation: These are different works rather than one work at twelve rotations, and the axis of difference is broadly the one the brief names - how far the mass has spread and how densely it packs. 9011, 9369 and 10801 are the tight quiet ones, 9548 and 10264 are the same recipe with the bone knot exploded into a wide radiating burst, 9190, 10443 and 10980 are crossed sticks at wide angles, 9727 adds its framing column. But the spread fails in both directions at once. At the near end 9011, 9369 and 10801 are close enough to be confusable with each other, a green peanut with a small bright smudge, three of twelve doing almost the same thing. At the far end 10622 has left the project entirely, and 9906 and 10085 have shed the defining element. A spread variant with zero cells is not a sparse colony, it is a missing one, and three tokens sit there.
thumbnailSurvival: At 120 the green peanut survives completely and is what tells one token from another; the bone cluster survives only as a bright smudge, and its slabs, rotations and overprinting all dissolve. Three silhouette families remain legible at browse size - compact knot in 9011, 9369, 10801, wide burst in 9548, 10264, crossed sticks in 9190, 10443, 10980 - plus 9727 by its square column and 10622 by being visibly foreign. Inside the families it collapses: 9011, 9369 and 10801 are one stamp at 120, and 10443 and 10980 are near enough to swap. So roughly five distinguishable things out of twelve at the size the collection is actually seen, which is where this frame loses most. The 256 sheets confirm the loss is real detail rather than mush - there is genuine slab structure at 256 that simply has nowhere to go at 120.
marketResponse: This is where the work fails against its own claim. The brief says recovery pushes the colony outward and multiplies its members, stress pulls it back toward the centre and reduces it, and that the change should be plainly visible at thumbnail size. Writing blind I recorded the opposite of the stress half: I noted that going neutral to stress the green mass generally grows and rounds out, its lobes separating into larger circles, and that in 9369 stress the two pale rectangles at left and right swell into big flat slabs and the knot slides outward - I called that the clearest single state change on the sheet, and it is an expansion, in the state that is supposed to contract. 9011 stress likewise carries a larger, rounder green mass than 9011 neutral. The recovery half fares better: 9548 recovery genuinely has more bone members reaching further out than 9548 neutral, and 9011 recovery fans wider. So one direction is weakly present and the other is absent or inverted. And the plainly visible at thumbnail requirement is not met at all: on the 120 state sheet 9011 neutral, stress and recovery read as the same picture nudged, 9190 likewise, and shuffled and unlabelled I could not sort those rows. Blind, I summarised the whole transition as the object breathing slightly rather than reacting. Growth and retreat is called the whole market story; what is on the sheet is a slight inflation and a reshuffle.
tokenIdentity: Unambiguously strong, and the one axis with no reservation. Every one of the four seeds shown across three states stays the same token: 9011 keeps its peanut, its upper-left knot and its two faint left-edge squares in all three; 9190 keeps its long crossed bars; 9369 keeps its tall twin-lobed body and small central knot; 9548 keeps its radiating burst on a rounder oval. Nothing is replaced by another object under drawdown and no state introduces a member type the others lack. It should be said plainly, though, that this axis passes partly for the reason marketResponse fails - identity is never threatened because the change is mild, so the strength here is bought with the weakness there.
artifacts: Real and specific. 10622 is cut hard by all four frame edges and reads as a crop rather than a composition. 9727 has its left-hand square column clipped by the left edge, so the framing device looks truncated rather than deliberate. In 9011 and 9369, in every state, pale rectangles sit half on and half off the green body at left and right and read as collisions rather than placements; in 9369 stress they swell and the accident gets louder. In 9906 and 10085 the near-total absence of the green mass reads as a layer that failed to draw. At 120 the centre of 9548 and 10264 packs into an undifferentiated bright blob where the individual slabs should be, losing the structure that is plainly there at 256. Nothing here is a render fault - it renders cleanly - but several of these read to a viewer as mistakes.
reasoning: The palette is genuinely good and the token identity is solid, but briefFidelity is a gate and this work is not the thing that was commissioned. The decisive evidence is that my blind description, written before I saw a word of the brief, used the exact vocabulary the brief rules out - I called the bone layer rotated rectangles, pick-up-sticks and asterisks, and 10622 slabs in horizontal courses - on a brief that asks for rounded forms and for a feeling biological rather than geometric. A colony of cells budding generation from generation is nowhere on the sheet: two or three lobes is not a colony, and in 9906, 10085 and 10622 there is no colony at all. Compounding that, the brief nominates growth and retreat as the whole market story and requires it to be plainly visible at thumbnail size, and blind I recorded the green mass getting larger under stress in 9011 and 9369 rather than retreating, and recorded that the 120px state rows for 9011 and 9190 could not be sorted if shuffled. Two of the briefs four demands fail, including the one it calls the whole story, and I am not refusing this for being an artwork I would have preferred otherwise - it is a handsome, competently made object whose green mass and overprinted mid-tones I would defend on their own terms. It is simply the answer to a different brief, and it would be on chain permanently.
wouldChange: Three concrete things. First, make the bone layer rounded: replace the rotated rectangles, slabs, squares and diamonds with discs, lozenges and lens shapes so the incident layer stops contradicting the word biological - this is the single change that would move the gate, because the palette already satisfies verdigris, bone and deep ink. Second, build an actual colony: instead of two or three big lobes, generate many small rounded members from a shared centre with each ring budding off the last at decreasing scale and increasing offset, so accretion is visible in the drawing rather than asserted in the brief, and put a floor under the member count so no seed can arrive with the mass missing the way 9906, 10085 and 10622 do. Third, invert and amplify the state response until it survives 120px: stress should cut member count hard and pull the survivors toward the centre so the silhouette visibly shrinks, recovery should raise the count and push the outer generation past the neutral radius, and the test should be that the three state rows of 9011 can be sorted correctly at 120px by silhouette area alone, with no labels - as it stands stress reads larger than neutral in 9011 and 9369, which is backwards. I would also cull one of 9011, 9369 and 10801 from the family, since at browse size they are one stamp.
